rationale: Evidence: every development trial so far ends off track, with max_error pinned at about 0.06 m (the off-track limit) and rms_error about 0.03 m. Progress ranges from 0.11 to 0.55, and the best design is iteration 5 (score 137.76). Several changes produced identical metrics to four decimals: kd 0.4 vs 1.0 (iterations 2 and 4), ki 0 vs 1.0 (iterations 5 and 6), and wheel_track 0.12 vs 0.10 (iterations 5 and 7). So gain and track-width tuning are not the binding limit at this geometry. The consistent 0.06 m excursion across all tracks and seeds points to a speed-limited failure: the robot cannot hold the tape through the bends at base_speed 1.3, and the lateral load pushes it past the limit. Change: lower base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1 to reduce lateral load and give the steering loop room to correct. Everything else is held at the iteration-7 values (geometry as iteration 5, wheel_track 0.10, kp 3.0, kd 0.4, ki 0, last_direction line loss), so the speed change is isolated. Expected result: fewer off-track ends, max_error below 0.06 for longer, and progress above the current 0.55 on the oval. Finishing within 3 s may be lost at this speed, but the progress and error terms carry most of the score, and a robot that stays on the line scores far more than one that leaves it. If progress rises clearly, the next step is a small speed increase to recover the finish-time term.
